newsitem.title: ITALY: Turin fire caused $35 million damage - experts.
newsitem.headline: Turin fire caused $35 million damage - experts.

text.p: A fire that destroyed part of Turin cathedral, home to the famous Turin shroud, and a section of an adjoining palace caused 60 billion lire ($35 million) of damage, art experts said on Thursday.

The experts, from the cultural heritage office of Italy's northern Piedmont region, said more than 80 works of art were also destroyed when the blaze swept through the buildings in the early hours of Saturday.
It gutted the baroque Guarini chapel, the home of the shroud at the back of Turin's Renaissance cathedral, and a tower of the city's Royal Palace.

"Of these 60 billion lire, 40 billion will be needed (to restore) the Chapel of the Holy Shroud and 20 for the Royal Palace," Pasquale Malara, the superintendent of architectural heritage for Piedmont, told a news conference.

Firemen managed to save the shroud, believed by many Roman Catholics to have wrapped the body of Christ after his crucifixion, after smashing through a protective bulletproof glass screen with a sledgehammer.
The winding cloth is kept in a silver case to save it from exposure to potentially damaging air pollution or sun light. Church staff say it suffered no damage.
Investigations are under way into what caused the blaze, which broke out shortly after a banquet at the palace in honour of visiting U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan.
The Italian government on Monday released 12 billion lire for initial restoration work.
Turin city council and the local region have earmarked 13 billion lire for the restoration and contributions have also been pouring in from local businesses and people in the city.
